The Saffire experiments were conducted in Orbital ATK's Cygnus vehicle after it had unberthed from the International Space Station. The vehicle was uncrewed, so large fires could be studied without risk to crew. The Saffire objectives were to determine how rapidly a large-scale fire grows in low gravity and to investigate low-g flammability limits compared with those from NASA's normal gravity material flammability screening test.

In SoFIE, a 0.1-mm-thick PMMA sample underwent radiative quenching when the flow velocity went below 2 cm/s (the evidence describes this as 'about 2 cm/s'). In the same figure, the flame neared blowoff extinction as the flow velocity crossed 40 cm/s.
Saffire-II sample 2-5 (5 cm wide cotton-fiberglass, 20 cm/s concurrent flow, about 22.1% O2, microgravity) burned its full 29 cm at a spread rate of 2.1 mm/s.

A principal objective of FLEX was to determine the limiting oxygen index (LOI), the oxygen percentage below which combustion would not occur. The report says this objective reflected the FLEX focus on investigating fire safety in spacecraft. The report states that observed LOI values for the FLEX fuels appear to be slightly lower than initially expected.

The FLEX authors report that a trace low-volatility contaminant was present in some FLEX tests. They judge that it had minimal influence on burning-rate constants: "Burning-rate constants were average, and the droplet history was minimally influenced by the contaminant." In FLEX, the 'burning rate' is the average burning-rate constant. It comes from a linear fit of droplet diameter squared versus time, from shortly after ignition to extinction.
